# How to use these scripts {: .nobreak}

These are the first 30 days of the Strong Years Daily Practice: 30 follow-along sessions, plus the guided monthly retest, with Chang Yin, 8 to 12 minutes each, in the weekly rotation members see in the app. **Monday strength, Tuesday mobility, Wednesday balance, Thursday strength, Friday breath and qigong, Saturday walk-and-talk, Sunday rest and stretch.**

Each session has:

- a **run of show** with minute marks and the dose for all four levels;
- the **full script**: every spoken line for Chang (and Sun Yoon's cameos), the time it lands, and the on-screen text;
- **cues, the easier and harder version, and safety callouts** for every move;
- **gentle-day swaps** for the app's "sore knee / sore back / low energy" button.

The same content is exported as `sessions.json` for the app and the video pipeline (one object per session, one object per segment, per-level variants, beats with timestamps).

## The four levels

| Level | Who it's for |
|---|---|
| **Rebuild** | Chair-based. Seated, or standing with both hands on the counter and the chair right behind you. Anyone who needs their hands to get out of a chair, uses a walker, or feels unsteady. If you can't stand safely at all, do every move seated and skip the standing balance holds. |
| **Steady** | Standard version with counter or wall support. Most new members. |
| **Strong** | Added load, slower lowering, less hand support. |
| **Iron** | For people who already train. Heavier, longer, some moves labelled advanced. Anything past 12 reps, 3 sets or 30-second holds is labelled **Advanced** on screen (SAFETY M-06). |

Move up a level only when a move feels easy for every rep in two sessions in a row. Moving down is always allowed, any day.

## Production rules baked into every script

- **Support cue within the first 10 seconds** of every movement (chair against the wall, counter, rail) — M-01.
- **Easier version** on screen for every movement — M-02. **Stop rule** on screen in the first 30 seconds and before hard blocks — M-03.
- **Breathing cue** in every strength move: breathe out on the effort; never "hold your breath" — M-04, E42.
- **Chang's level** demonstrations carry the label "Chang's level — not your starting point" — M-07.
- Chairs shown against a wall; balance next to a counter; shoes on; no rugs; no socks on hard floors — M-09, M-10.
- Every generated movement clip passes human form review before publishing (knees track over toes, neutral spine on hinges, chair doesn't slide) — M-08.
- The "AI character" corner tag is on screen the whole time — D-02. Caption ends with the movement add-on and the disclosure footer — D-03.

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Before members start:</span> the app runs the safety screen (chest pain, fainting, recent surgery or fracture, a doctor's limit on activity) and routes those members to the Rebuild level with a note to show their doctor the plan (E43). Stop if you feel chest pain or pressure, dizziness, unusual shortness of breath, or sharp pain. Chest pain, face drooping, arm weakness or trouble speaking? Call 911 now. Pain rule: Mild discomfort up to 3 out of 10 is okay if it settles by tomorrow. Sharper, or worse the next day: back off and ask your doctor or physical therapist.
</div>

<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Sit-to-stand from a higher seat (cushion) and only halfway down; swap the wall sit for seated knee straightening. **Sore back:** Keep the row upright with the towel pull-apart instead of the hinged jug row. **Low energy:** Do one set of everything and the cool-down. ### 0:35–0:55 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down first. Toes away, toes to you.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wake up the calves. They pump blood back up.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:55–1:35 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rebuild, stay seated. Everyone else, stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Talk to me if you want. I'm listening. Sort of.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–1:55 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders up. Back. Down.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in up, breathe out down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:55–4:15 · Chair sit-to-stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Sit in the middle. Feet flat, a little behind your knees.</td><td>Chair sit-to-stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes. Push the floor away. Stand tall.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down slow. The chair is farther away than you think.</td><td>Breathe out as you stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Knees over toes</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rest. Shake the legs. Next set when you're ready.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees point where your toes point. Good.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:15–6:05 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Now arms. Rebuild, sit and press forward. Steady and Strong, the wall. Iron, the counter.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Body in one straight line. Chest to the wall, not your chin.</td><td>Easier: Closer to wall, half range</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push away.</td><td>Breathe out as you push</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Muscle is a savings account. Deposit now.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Body in one straight line, head to heels. Chest to the wall, not your chin. **Easier:** Stand closer to the wall and move only halfway. **Harder:** Step your feet farther back. When 15 are easy, move to counter push-ups.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:05–7:05 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Up on your toes. Pause. Down for three.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Calves are your second heart pump. Treat them nicely.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:05–8:45 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Now pull. Hand on the counter. Long back.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull with your elbow, not your hand.</td><td>Easier: Towel pull or lighter jug</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull. Lower slow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Switch sides.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Pull with your elbow, not your hand. Long back. Don't twist. **Easier:** Stand upright and pull a towel looped around a sturdy door handle (see Towel row), or use a lighter jug. **Harder:** Full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), or a bag with a few cans. Pause for one second at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:40 · Finisher

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Last one. Back on the wall. Slide down a few inches. Chair beside you.</td><td>Finisher</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Keep breathing. Count out loud with me. Talking means you're not holding your breath.</td><td>Easier: Only 2 inches down, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>High blood pressure or a heart condition? Keep it short and ask your doctor about long holds.</td><td>Keep breathing: count out loud | High BP? Ask your doctor before long holds | Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shallow is fine. This is not a contest of depth. Knees stay behind or over your toes. **Easier:** Slide down only 2 inches, or hold for just 10 seconds. **Harder:** Slide a little lower (never below where your knees are bent to a right angle), or hold up to 30 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Breathe through it. High blood pressure or a heart condition? Ask your doctor before long holds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:40–10:50 · Cool-down

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the wall. One foot back. Heel down.</td><td>Cool-down</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slow.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Now sit. Two sniffs in through the nose, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:50–11:15 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>That's Day 1. Write your number in the log.</td><td>Log today's session</td></tr>
<tr><td>11:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Strong is a habit. Same time tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

### 0:35–1:05 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Toes away, toes back. Then circles.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:05–1:50 · Neck nods and half-turns

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Neck nods and half-turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nod yes. Small. Slow.</td><td>Easier: Even smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn right, only as far as comfortable. Back. Left.</td><td>Nods and half-turns only</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>No big circles with the neck. Ever. Nods and half-turns.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small and slow. Chin stays level when you turn. **Easier:** Make the movement even smaller. **Harder:** Add a chin tuck: gently slide your chin straight back, making a double chin, hold two seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Dizzy with head movements? Keep it tiny, keep your eyes open, and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:50–2:30 · Chest lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit near the front of the chair. Lift your chest. Grow tall.</td><td>Chest lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift. Out as you relax.</td><td>Easier: Smaller lift</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall. Look straight ahead, not up. **Easier:** Smaller lift. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:30–3:20 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Arms crossed. Grow tall first. Then turn.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn. Only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Osteoporosis: small and gentle</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Osteoporosis? Small and gentle. Never force it.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:20–4:20 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>One leg straight. Heel down. Toes up.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Hinge from the hips. Not the belly.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slow. A gentle stretch is enough.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:20–5:10 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle on the other knee, or on the shin. Sit tall.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let the knee relax. Don't push it.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions. Skip this one if they said no crossing.</td><td>New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:10–6:10 · Standing hip-front stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hand on the counter. Small step back.</td><td>Standing hip-front stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuck the tailbone. Squeeze the back buttock.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slow. Switch.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:02</td><td>Sun</td><td>He skips this one when I'm not home. I'm always home.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Don't arch your back. Small movement, big squeeze. **Easier:** Smaller step. **Harder:** Reach the arm on the back-leg side up toward the ceiling, to comfortable height.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:10–6:55 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. One foot back. Heel down.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:55–7:45 · Standing bird-dog

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Both hands on the counter. Slide one foot back.</td><td>Standing bird-dog</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Reach the other arm forward if you're steady.</td><td>Easier: Leg only, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Long back. No arching. Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg. **Easier:** Leg only; both hands stay on the counter. **Harder:** Hold the reach for three seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:45–8:25 · Wall slides

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back on the wall. Arms like a goalpost.</td><td>Wall slides</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide up only as far as comfortable. Ribs down.</td><td>Easier: Walk fingertips up the wall</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you slide up, out as you slide down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Slow and smooth. **Easier:** Face the wall and walk your fingertips up it instead. **Harder:** Hold for two seconds at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:25–9:25 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. In for four. Out for six. No holding.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>About six breaths a minute. Slow breathing like this raises heart-rate variability while you do it.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:25–9:50 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>That's mobility. Sun says seven out of ten.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow, balance. Same time.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:42</td><td>Sun</td><td>Seven. Because I love you.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# Session 3 · Wednesday: Steady feet

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balance | 8:55 | SET-KITCHEN | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Keep feet wider and holds shorter; skip the heel-to-toe walk. **Sore back:** Skip the clock reach behind you; reach front and side only. **Low energy:** Weight shifts, heel-to-toe stand and one-leg stand only.
</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wednesday. Balance. We live at the counter today.</td><td>Day 3 · Balance</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoes on. No rugs. Chair right behind you.</td><td>Stand at the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover. They don't wander.</td><td>Stop if dizzy</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Dizzy? Sit down. Tell your doctor if it keeps happening.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:20 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Both hands on the counter. Shift right. Pause. Shift left.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Like a tree in wind. Feet stay flat.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:20–2:35 · Heel-to-toe stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. One foot in front of the other. Heel to toe.</td><td>Heel-to-toe stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes on something still. Soft knees.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Ten, nine, eight...</td><td>Hands hover, they don't wander</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Switch feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rebuild: half a step, both hands down. That's real practice.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:50 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Weight on the left foot. Lift the right a few inches.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Count out loud. Breathe.</td><td>Chang's level — not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>This is my level. Thirty seconds, hands hovering, right beside the counter. Not your starting point.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:50–4:50 · Heel-to-toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>One hand on the counter. Heel in front of toes. Ten steps.</td><td>Heel-to-toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes forward. Slow is correct.</td><td>Easier: Feet apart, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn carefully. Walk back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes forward, not down at your feet. Slow is correct. **Easier:** Walk with your feet slightly apart, not touching, holding the counter. **Harder:** Let your hand hover above the counter. Later: walk backward along the counter with one hand resting on it (normal steps).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:50–5:40 · Side steps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Face the counter. Step right. Feet meet. Ten steps.</td><td>Side steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes forward. Stay tall. Back to the left.</td><td>Easier: Fewer, slower steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally. Talk or count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Small, controlled steps. Feet don't cross. **Easier:** Fewer steps, slower. **Harder:** Bend your knees slightly and stay low, or tie a resistance loop above your knees.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:40–6:30 · Sit-to-stand, no hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Stand. Find your balance at the top. Two seconds.</td><td>Sit-to-stand, no hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Sit slow.</td><td>Easier: Hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Find your balance at the top before you move. Slow down. **Easier:** Use your hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Feet together.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:30–7:20 · Clock reach

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Side-on to the counter. Near hand down.</td><td>Clock reach</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Reach to twelve o'clock. Back. Three o'clock. Back.</td><td>Easier: Smaller reaches, front and side</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Behind you, only as far as comfortable. Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Follow your hand with your eyes. Feet stay planted. **Easier:** Smaller reaches, and only to the front and side. **Harder:** Stand on one foot while you reach to 12 o'clock, holding the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:20–8:00 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Both hands on the counter. Up. Pause. Down for three.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:00–8:30 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing | Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:30–8:55 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good. Balance is a skill. Skills get better with practice.</td><td>Tonight: toothbrush balance</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Brush your teeth heel-to-toe tonight. Hand on the sink.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# Session 4 · Thursday: Push, pull, carry

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Strength | 11:15 | SET-GARAGE | C-TRAIN-A | Chang, Sun |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Thursday. Second strength day.</td><td>Day 4 · Strength</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Today we stand up faster. Not sloppy. Faster.</td><td>Fast up, slow down</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lifting quick and lowering slow helps older adults move better in daily life, in the research.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Bottom stair with a rail, if you have one. Stop if anything feels wrong.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · March

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. March. Warm up the hips.</td><td>March</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steady. You should be able to talk.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:40 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Up, back, down. Breathe in up, out down.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:40–2:10 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Five easy ones. Just waking the legs.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:10–4:00 · Power stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Pop up. Stand tall one second. Lower for three.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fast up, slow down. Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>If standing fast makes you dizzy, go back to normal speed.</td><td>Dizzy? Normal speed</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Getting up quick is what saves you when you trip. Legs first.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:00–5:50 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bottom stair. Hand on the rail. The whole time.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on the step. Push through the heel.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up. Step down slow.</td><td>Rail hand stays on the rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rebuild: stay seated, knees high. Same muscles.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:50–7:10 · Hinge

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Hips back like closing a car door.</td><td>Hinge</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Chest proud. No rounding.</td><td>Easier: Smaller hinge, hands stay down</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze your buttocks to stand. Breathe out.</td><td>Long back. No rounding.</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Osteoporosis? This is the safe way to bend. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips go back, not down. Long back, chest proud. No rounding. Stand up by squeezing your buttocks. **Easier:** Smaller movement, hands stay on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** Pick up a jug of water from the seat of a chair using the same hinge, and set it back down. Later: from a lower surface, like a step.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: this is the safe way to bend. Keep your back long; never round forward under load.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:10–8:10 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Elbows by your sides. Curl up. Lower slow.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Yes, I'm flexing. Sun, don't look.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:02</td><td>Sun</td><td>NO MIRROR FLEXING.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:10–9:10 · Carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pick the bags up with a hinge. Long back.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Short steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Put them down the same way. Hinge.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:10–9:50 · Towel wring

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Towel wring</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wring it like laundry. Three seconds.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze a rolled sock</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Squeeze from your whole hand, not just your fingertips. Shoulders relaxed. **Easier:** Squeeze a soft ball or rolled sock instead. **Harder:** Use a damp towel, or hold each wring for five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:50–10:50 · Cool-down

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Lift the chest. Relax.</td><td>Cool-down</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in. Long sigh out. Twice more.</td><td>Easier: Smaller lift</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall. Look straight ahead, not up. **Easier:** Smaller lift. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:50–11:15 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push, pull, carry. That's daily life. You trained it.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>11:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>One more. A good one. Tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Friday. Breath and flow.</td><td>Day 5 · Breath + qigong</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tai chi and qigong are exercise. That's how we teach them. Movement you can measure.</td><td>Chair behind you</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Today: slow breathing, then five pieces of a qigong set called baduanjin.</td><td>Stop if dizzy or chest pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>We skip two pieces. They round the spine and put your head below your heart. Not for everyone. So not for us.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair behind you. Sit down anytime.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stop if you feel dizzy, light-headed or any chest pain.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–2:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit comfortably. Breathe in through the nose.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>At the top, sip a little more air.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Now a long, slow sigh out through the mouth.</td><td>2 sniffs in · 1 long sigh out</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding. Ever. The out-breath is longer.</td><td>No breath holds</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>In a one-month study, five minutes of this a day lifted mood more than meditation.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Light-headed? Go back to normal breathing.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:35 · Holding up the sky

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Holding up the sky</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Fingers laced at your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in. Hands float up. Palms to the sky.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Only to comfortable height. Breathe out. Arms float down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow, like moving through warm water. Look straight ahead. **Easier:** Sit and do it seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Rise onto your toes a little at the top, holding the chair back with one hand if needed.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:35–4:35 · Drawing the bow

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Drawing the bow</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet a little wide. High stance. Not a squat.</td><td>Easier: Seated, arms only</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push the left hand out. Pull the right elbow back. Eyes follow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you draw. Switch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Knees over toes. Grow tall through the top of the head. **Easier:** Sit tall in your chair and do the arm movement only. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more (never below comfortable).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:35–5:35 · Separating heaven and earth

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Separating heaven and earth</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>One hand presses up. One presses down.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you separate. Out as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulder sore? Only to shoulder height.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** One hand reaches up, one presses down. Long spine. **Easier:** Seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Slower, with a longer out-breath.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:25 · Looking back

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand or sit tall. Turn your head, only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Looking back</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chin level. Shoulders down. Half-turns only.</td><td>Easier: Turn the eyes more</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn, in as you return.</td><td>Half-turns only</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chin level. Shoulders stay down. **Easier:** Turn your eyes more than your head. **Harder:** Hold the turn for one slow breath.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:15 · Punching with a steady gaze

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Punching with a steady gaze</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Loose fists at the waist. Slow punch forward. Turn the palm down.</td><td>Easier: Seated, same arm movement</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Open, grip the air, pull it back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you punch. This is not boxing. Sun asked.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow punch. This is not boxing. Eyes steady and focused. **Easier:** Seated, same arm movement. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more, keeping them over your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:15 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight right. Right hand floats past your face.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift left. The hands switch. Like wiping a big window.</td><td>Soft knees, slow shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call this sinking. Really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow weight shifts like this are balance practice. And balance is one of the most trainable things there is.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:15–9:15 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. In for four. Out for six.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>No pause at the top. No pause at the bottom.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

### 0:35–1:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in through the nose. Long sigh out.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–2:15 · Neck nods and half-turns

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Neck nods and half-turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small nods. Half-turns. Slow.</td><td>Easier: Even smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small and slow. Chin stays level when you turn. **Easier:** Make the movement even smaller. **Harder:** Add a chin tuck: gently slide your chin straight back, making a double chin, hold two seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Dizzy with head movements? Keep it tiny, keep your eyes open, and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:15–2:45 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Up, back, down.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:45–3:30 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall first. Then turn. Only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:30–4:30 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Leg straight. Long back. Hinge from the hips.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:30–5:20 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle on knee or shin. Sit tall. Let it relax.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>New hip? Your surgeon's rules first.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–6:05 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hands on the counter. Heel down.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:05–6:50 · Bed bridge (optional)

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Optional. On your bed. Knees bent. Squeeze and lift a few inches.</td><td>Bed bridge (optional)</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you lift.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze without lifting</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand. Then stand slowly, holding something.</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Push through your heels. Lift with your buttocks, not your back. **Easier:** Just squeeze your buttocks without lifting. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top, or lift higher.

**Safety callouts:** Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:50–7:20 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Seated. Toes away, toes to you. Before you stand, every time.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:20–8:20 · Week check-in

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<tr><td>7:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Your full Strength Age retest is on day 30. Not today.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:20–8:50 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Week two. Monday. Strength.</td><td>Day 8 · Strength</td></tr>

<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Counter close.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stop if you feel chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:20 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle pumps first if you've been sitting. Then stand slowly.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Hand on the counter.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:20–1:50 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Five easy. Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:50–4:00 · Legs

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Legs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Three sets today. Nose over toes. Push the floor away.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down slow. Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Iron: advanced</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Iron: split squat at the counter. Straight down, like an elevator.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rest. Next set.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Advanced. Only if your knees feel good with step-ups.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:00–5:50 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Strong: move to the counter this week.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Straight line head to heels. Breathe out as you push.</td><td>Easier: Closer to wall, half range</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Body in one straight line, head to heels. Chest to the wall, not your chin. **Easier:** Stand closer to the wall and move only halfway. **Harder:** Step your feet farther back. When 15 are easy, move to counter push-ups.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:50–6:50 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Up. Pause. Down for three.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:50–8:30 · Row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Long back. Pull with the elbow.</td><td>Row</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td>Easier: Towel pull or lighter jug</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Pull with your elbow, not your hand. Long back. Don't twist. **Easier:** Stand upright and pull a towel looped around a sturdy door handle (see Towel row), or use a lighter jug. **Harder:** Full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), or a bag with a few cans. Pause for one second at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: keep the hinge small and the back long.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:30–9:30 · Press

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Bottles at the shoulders.</td><td>Press</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press up only to comfortable height. Ribs down.</td><td>Easier: One arm, press at a slant</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulder sore? Press forward at a slant, or skip it today.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you press up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Don't arch your back. Only to comfortable height. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or press forward and up at a slant instead of straight up. **Harder:** Heavier bottles or a half-gallon jug in each hand; stand at the counter to press.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:30–10:25 · Finisher

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back on the wall. A few inches down.</td><td>Finisher</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Count out loud. Keep breathing.</td><td>Easier: Only 2 inches down, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>High blood pressure? Short holds, and ask your doctor about long ones.</td><td>Keep breathing: count out loud | Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shallow is fine. This is not a contest of depth. Knees stay behind or over your toes. **Easier:** Slide down only 2 inches, or hold for just 10 seconds. **Harder:** Slide a little lower (never below where your knees are bent to a right angle), or hold up to 30 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Breathe through it. High blood pressure or a heart condition? Ask your doctor before long holds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:25–11:25 · Cool-down

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Calf stretch at the wall. Then sit. Two sniffs in, long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down | Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 11:25–11:50 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>11:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>One more set than last week. That's the whole game.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>11:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Deposit made. Same time tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Slide your chin straight back. Double chin. Beautiful.</td><td>Chin tucks</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes level. Breathe normally.</td><td>Easier: Smaller, 1-second hold</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slide back, don't tip down. Tall neck. **Easier:** Smaller movement, one-second hold. **Harder:** Hold five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:45 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big slow circles backward.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–2:35 · Wall slides

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back to the wall. Goalpost arms.</td><td>Wall slides</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide up only as far as comfortable. Breathe out as you slide down.</td><td>Easier: Walk fingertips up the wall</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Slow and smooth. **Easier:** Face the wall and walk your fingertips up it instead. **Harder:** Hold for two seconds at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:15 · Chest lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Near the front of the chair. Lift the chest. Grow tall.</td><td>Chest lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you relax.</td><td>Easier: Smaller lift</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall. Look straight ahead, not up. **Easier:** Smaller lift. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:15–4:05 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall. Turn. Only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Osteoporosis: small and gentle.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:05–5:05 · Standing hip-front stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the fence or counter. Small step back.</td><td>Standing hip-front stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuck, squeeze, shift forward a little.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Don't arch your back. Small movement, big squeeze. **Easier:** Smaller step. **Harder:** Reach the arm on the back-leg side up toward the ceiling, to comfortable height.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–5:55 · Standing bird-dog

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Both hands on the fence. Foot back. Arm forward if steady.</td><td>Standing bird-dog</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Breathe out as you reach.</td><td>Easier: Leg only, both hands down</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Long back. No arching. Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg. **Easier:** Leg only; both hands stay on the counter. **Harder:** Hold the reach for three seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:55–6:45 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Ankle on the knee or shin. Relax the knee.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>New hip? Your surgeon's precautions first.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:45–7:35 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Leg straight, heel down. Long back. Hinge from the hips.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:35–8:35 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for four. Out for six. No holds.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:35–9:00 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Done. My shoulders say thank you. I won't tell Sun.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow: balance.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:52</td><td>Sun</td><td>I heard that.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# Session 10 · Wednesday: Steadier feet

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balance | 9:10 | SET-KITCHEN | C-TRAIN-B | Chang, Sun |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">
<span class="label">On screen the whole session:</span> the "AI character" corner tag. In the first 30 seconds and before each hard block: "Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain."
</div>

<div class="box note" markdown="1">
<span class="label">Gentle-day swaps (the sore knee / sore back / low energy button):</span> **Sore knee:** Shorter holds, wider feet; skip the backward walk. **Sore back:** Front and side reaches only. **Low energy:** Heel-to-toe stand, one-leg stand, cloud hands.
</div>
