<tr><td>0:35–1:15</td><td><strong>Weight shifts</strong></td><td>5 each way, seated</td><td>6 each way</td><td>8 each way, bigger</td><td>8 each way, one hand hovering</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:15–2:30</td><td><strong>Heel-to-toe stand</strong><br>Heel-to-toe stand at the counter</td><td>3 × 15 seconds each side, half-step, both hands down</td><td>3 × 15 seconds each side</td><td>3 × 20 seconds each side, hands hovering</td><td>3 × 30 seconds each side, hands hovering</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:30–3:45</td><td><strong>One-leg stand</strong><br>One-leg stand at the counter</td><td>3 × 10 seconds each side, toe down</td><td>3 × 15 seconds each side</td><td>3 × 20 seconds each side, one hand hovering</td><td>3 × 30 seconds each side, hands hovering</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:45–4:45</td><td><strong>Heel-to-toe walk</strong><br>Heel-to-toe walk along the counter</td><td>2 lengths, feet apart, holding on</td><td>3 lengths</td><td>2 lengths forward + 1 backward, hand on the counter</td><td>2 forward, hand hovering + 2 backward, hand on the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:45–5:35</td><td><strong>Side steps</strong><br>Side steps along the counter</td><td>1 set of 8 each way</td><td>2 sets of 10 each way, knees bent</td><td>2 sets of 12 each way, knees bent</td><td>3 sets of 12 each way, knees bent</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:35–6:25</td><td><strong>Sit-to-stand, no hands</strong><br>Sit-to-stand without hands (balance version)</td><td><em>Chair sit-to-stand:</em> 1 set of 6, hands on thighs</td><td>1 set of 8</td><td>2 sets of 6, feet together</td><td>2 sets of 8, feet together, 3-second lower</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:25–7:15</td><td><strong>Clock reach</strong></td><td>3 each way, front and side</td><td>4 each direction</td><td>4 each direction, one foot at 12</td><td>5 each direction, one foot at 12</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15–8:15</td><td><strong>Cloud hands</strong><br>Cloud hands (tai chi, simplified)</td><td>1 minute, seated</td><td>1 minute</td><td>1 minute</td><td>1 minute with side steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:15–8:45</td><td><strong>Cyclic sighing</strong></td><td>30 seconds</td><td>30 seconds</td><td>30 seconds</td><td>30 seconds</td></tr>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wednesday. Balance, week two.</td><td>Day 10 · Balance</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Holds get longer today. Support stays the same. Counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Balance is trainable</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Balance is one of the most trainable things there is. Practise it and you feel steadier on your feet, and more confident on stairs.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Dizzy? Sit down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Side to side. Front to back.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:30 · Heel-to-toe stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Heel to toe. Hands on the counter, or hovering if you're Strong or Iron.</td><td>Heel-to-toe stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes on something still. Breathe.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Switch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:30–3:45 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight on one foot. Lift the other.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Count out loud. Squeeze the standing buttock.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Switch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:45–4:45 · Heel-to-toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Heel in front of toes.</td><td>Heel-to-toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Backward walk for Strong and Iron: normal steps, slow, hand resting on the counter.</td><td>Easier: Feet apart, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes forward, not down at your feet. Slow is correct. **Easier:** Walk with your feet slightly apart, not touching, holding the counter. **Harder:** Let your hand hover above the counter. Later: walk backward along the counter with one hand resting on it (normal steps).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:45–5:35 · Side steps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Face the counter. Knees a little bent. Step, feet meet.</td><td>Side steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:08</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally. Talk or count out loud.</td><td>Easier: Fewer, slower steps</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Small, controlled steps. Feet don't cross. **Easier:** Fewer steps, slower. **Harder:** Bend your knees slightly and stay low, or tie a resistance loop above your knees.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:25 · Sit-to-stand, no hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand. Balance two seconds at the top. Sit slow.</td><td>Sit-to-stand, no hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Find your balance at the top before you move. Slow down. **Easier:** Use your hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Feet together.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:15 · Clock reach

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Side-on to the counter. Reach to the clock numbers. Eyes follow the hand.</td><td>Clock reach</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you reach.</td><td>Easier: Smaller reaches, front and side</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Follow your hand with your eyes. Feet stay planted. **Easier:** Smaller reaches, and only to the front and side. **Harder:** Stand on one foot while you reach to 12 o'clock, holding the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:15 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift and float. Right, then left.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft knees. Center of mass low.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:15–8:45 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Two sniffs in. Long sigh out.</td><td>Cyclic sighing | Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:10 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Update the fridge chart. Longest one-leg time.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sun's number is still better. For now.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:02</td><td>Sun</td><td>For always.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">

<tr><td>3:35–5:25</td><td><strong>Step-ups</strong><br>Step-ups on the bottom stair</td><td><em>Seated march:</em> 3 × 30 seconds, knees high</td><td>2 sets of 6 each leg</td><td>3 sets of 6 each leg</td><td>3 sets of 8 each leg, bag in free hand (advanced)</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:25–6:45</td><td><strong>Hinge pick-up</strong><br>Counter hip hinge</td><td><em>Seated hip hinge:</em> 2 sets of 8</td><td>2 sets of 8, jug from the chair seat</td><td>3 sets of 8, jug from the chair seat</td><td>3 sets of 8, heavier bag from the bottom step</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:45–7:55</td><td><strong>Push</strong><br>Wall push-up</td><td><em>Seated chest press:</em> 2 sets of 10</td><td>2 sets of 10, feet farther back</td><td><em>Counter push-up:</em> 2 sets of 10</td><td><em>Counter push-up:</em> 3 sets of 10, 3-second lower</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:55–8:50</td><td><strong>Curls</strong><br>Water-bottle curl</td><td>2 sets of 10, bottles</td><td>2 sets of 10, half-gallon jug</td><td>3 sets of 10, half-gallon jug</td><td>3 sets of 10, gallon jug</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:50–10:00</td><td><strong>Carry</strong><br>Grocery carry</td><td><em>Towel wring (grip):</em> 4 wrings each direction</td><td>2 walks of 30 seconds, two bags</td><td>3 walks of 30 seconds, heavier bags</td><td>3 walks of 45 seconds, heavy bags</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:00–10:50</td><td><strong>Cool-down</strong><br>Seated chest lift</td><td>6 lifts</td><td>6 lifts</td><td>6 lifts</td><td>6 lifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:50–11:15</td><td><strong>Close</strong></td><td colspan="4">All levels together</td></tr>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Thursday. Strength, week two.</td><td>Day 11 · Strength</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Three sets on the big moves. Fast up, slow down.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Stair rail. Counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. March.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:45 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Five easy. Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–3:35 · Power stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pop up. Stand tall. Lower for three.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Dizzy when you stand fast? Normal speed.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:35–5:25 · Step-ups

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the rail the whole time.</td><td>Step-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Steady: real step-ups this week. Whole foot on the step.</td><td>Easier: Toe taps, hand on rail</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you step up.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step, not just the toes. Push through the heel of the top foot. Rail hand stays on the rail. **Easier:** Toe taps: tap the step with one foot, then the other, holding the rail. Or use a lower step, like a sturdy doorway threshold. **Harder:** Step up without pushing off the bottom foot. Later: carry a light bag of groceries in the hand that isn't on the rail.

**Safety callouts:** If stairs make you dizzy or you have fallen on stairs, do toe taps only until you've practiced balance for two weeks.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:25–6:45 · Hinge pick-up

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Hinge pick-up</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back. Pick up the jug.</td><td>Easier: Smaller hinge, hands stay down</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze to stand. Breathe out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Put it down the same way.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips go back, not down. Long back, chest proud. No rounding. Stand up by squeezing your buttocks. **Easier:** Smaller movement, hands stay on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** Pick up a jug of water from the seat of a chair using the same hinge, and set it back down. Later: from a lower surface, like a step.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: this is the safe way to bend. Keep your back long; never round forward under load.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:45–7:55 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wall in front of you or behind you. Chair nearby.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>One straight line. Breathe out as you push.</td><td>Easier: Closer to wall, half range</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Body in one straight line, head to heels. Chest to the wall, not your chin. **Easier:** Stand closer to the wall and move only halfway. **Harder:** Step your feet farther back. When 15 are easy, move to counter push-ups.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:55–8:50 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows by your sides. Curl. Lower slow.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:50–10:00 · Carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hinge to pick up. Stand tall. Short steps.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe. Hinge to put down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:00–10:50 · Cool-down

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Chest up. Two sniffs in, long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down | Easier: Smaller lift</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall. Look straight ahead, not up. **Easier:** Smaller lift. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:50–11:15 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>I'm made of pixels. Your muscles are made of protein. Go eat some.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>11:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow: breath and flow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Friday. Breath and flow. Six pieces today.</td><td>Day 12 · Breath + qigong</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>New piece at the end: rise up on the toes. Most of us lower slowly. No jumping.</td><td>Stop if dizzy or chest pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair behind you.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Light-headed, dizzy, or chest pain? Stop and sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–2:05 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in. Long sigh out.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding. If you feel light-headed, breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–3:00 · Holding up the sky

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Holding up the sky</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands rise with the in-breath. Float down with the out-breath.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow, like moving through warm water. Look straight ahead. **Easier:** Sit and do it seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Rise onto your toes a little at the top, holding the chair back with one hand if needed.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:00–3:55 · Drawing the bow

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Drawing the bow</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>High stance. Push out. Draw back. Breathe out as you draw.</td><td>Easier: Seated, arms only</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Knees over toes. Grow tall through the top of the head. **Easier:** Sit tall in your chair and do the arm movement only. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more (never below comfortable).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:55–4:50 · Separating heaven and earth

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Separating heaven and earth</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>One hand up, one hand down. Long spine.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you separate, out as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** One hand reaches up, one presses down. Long spine. **Easier:** Seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Slower, with a longer out-breath.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:50–5:35 · Looking back

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Looking back</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Half-turns only. Chin level.</td><td>Easier: Turn the eyes more</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn, in as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chin level. Shoulders stay down. **Easier:** Turn your eyes more than your head. **Harder:** Hold the turn for one slow breath.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:25 · Punching with a steady gaze

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Punching with a steady gaze</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow punch. Grip the air. Pull back. Breathe out as you punch.</td><td>Easier: Seated, same arm movement</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow punch. This is not boxing. Eyes steady and focused. **Easier:** Seated, same arm movement. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more, keeping them over your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:15 · Heel raise and gentle drop

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Up on the toes.</td><td>Heel raise and gentle drop</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:38</td><td>Chang</td><td>Most of you: lower slowly. Strong and Iron: a soft bump.</td><td>Easier: Slow lower, no drop</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Osteoporosis without a training history, pelvic floor problems, or a joint replacement? No drop. Slow lower.</td><td>Gentle impact — slow lower if unsure</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you rise, out as you lower.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall spine. Soft bump, never a stomp. **Easier:** Heel raise with a slow lower, no drop. **Harder:** Ten gentle drops.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today. Gentle impact. Skip it if you have osteoporosis without a training history, pelvic floor problems, or a joint replacement; do the heel raise without the drop instead.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:15 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift and float. Like wiping a big window.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:15–9:15 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for four. Out for six.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:15–9:40 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Six pieces. Well done.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow we walk. Longer brisk bits.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

### 6:35–7:20 · Bench stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Find a sturdy bench, or your chair at home.</td><td>Bench stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand up. Sit down slow. Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sunday. Two weeks done.</td><td>Day 14 · Rest + stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretches. Then a look back, and a look ahead.</td><td>Stop if sharp pain or dizziness</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Log and pencil nearby.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Anything sharp, or dizziness? Stop and sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in. Long sigh out.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–2:05 · Chin tucks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Chin tucks</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide the chin back. Eyes level.</td><td>Easier: Smaller, 1-second hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slide back, don't tip down. Tall neck. **Easier:** Smaller movement, one-second hold. **Harder:** Hold five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–2:35 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Up, back, down.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:20 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, then turn. Only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:20–4:20 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. Hinge. Breathe.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:20–5:10 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle on knee or shin. Relax. New hip: surgeon's rules first.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:10–5:55 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand slowly. Hands on the counter. Heel down.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:55–6:40 · Bed bridge (optional)

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Optional. On the bed. Squeeze and lift.</td><td>Bed bridge (optional)</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand. Then stand slowly, holding something.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze without lifting</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you lift.</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Push through your heels. Lift with your buttocks, not your back. **Easier:** Just squeeze your buttocks without lifting. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top, or lift higher.

**Safety callouts:** Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:40–7:55 · Two-week check-in

</tbody></table>

<tr><td>5:05–6:25</td><td><strong>Push</strong><br>Wall push-up</td><td><em>Seated chest press:</em> 2 sets of 10</td><td>2 sets of 10, feet back</td><td><em>Counter push-up:</em> 3 sets of 8</td><td><em>Counter push-up:</em> 3 sets of 12, 3-second lower</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:25–7:35</td><td><strong>Band row</strong><br>Seated band row</td><td><em>Seated towel pull-apart:</em> 4 pulls, 3-second squeeze</td><td>2 sets of 10</td><td>3 sets of 10</td><td>3 sets of 12, 2-second pause</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:35–9:05</td><td><strong>Floor practice</strong><br>Floor practice with a chair (kneel and rise)</td><td><em>Chair sit-to-stand:</em> 1 set of 5 (no floor today)</td><td>2 half-kneels each side, holding the chair</td><td>2 kneel-and-rise, holding the chair</td><td>2 sit-to-floor and rise, someone home</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:05–9:50</td><td><strong>Heel raises</strong><br>Heel raises at the counter</td><td>2 sets of 12, seated</td><td>2 sets of 12</td><td>2 sets of 12, one hand</td><td>2 sets of 10 each leg</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:50–10:35</td><td><strong>Calf stretch</strong><br>Calf stretch at the wall</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:35–11:10</td><td><strong>Cool-down breathing</strong><br>Cyclic sighing</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td></tr>
<tr><td>11:10–11:35</td><td><strong>Close</strong></td><td colspan="4">All levels together</td></tr>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Week three. Monday. New move today: the floor.</td><td>Day 15 · Strength</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Getting down and up is a skill. Practise it before you ever need it.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Someone else home for that part. Sturdy chair next to you. Towel for your knee.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness, sharp pain: stop and sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle pumps first if you've been sitting. Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:45 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Five easy ones.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–3:45 · Legs

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Three sets.</td><td>Legs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes. Push the floor away. Sit down slow.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Advanced. Only if your knees feel good with step-ups.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:45–5:05 · Suitcase lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Suitcase lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back with a long back and bend your knees a little.</td><td>Easier: Lighter jug, higher surface</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips back. Long back. Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square. **Easier:** A lighter jug, and lift it from a higher surface like the counter's edge of a table. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or lift from the bottom step instead of the chair.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: long back always, never round to reach.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–6:25 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wall in front of you or behind you. Chair nearby.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring your chest toward the wall.</td><td>Easier: Closer to wall, half range</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Body in one straight line, head to heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest to the wall, not your chin.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push away.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Body in one straight line, head to heels. Chest to the wall, not your chin. **Easier:** Stand closer to the wall and move only halfway. **Harder:** Step your feet farther back. When 15 are easy, move to counter push-ups.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:35 · Band row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band row</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull your elbows back past your ribs.</td><td>Easier: Closer to the door, or towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows close to your body.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall chest, shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows close to your body. Tall chest, shoulders down. **Easier:** Sit closer to the door so the band is slacker, or do the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Scoot back for more tension, or pause 2 seconds with elbows back.

**Safety callouts:** Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:35–9:05 · Floor practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair or sofa right beside you. Towel down. Someone else is home.</td><td>Floor practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step back. Lower one knee to the towel. Hands on the chair.</td><td>Easier: Half-kneel only, or chair stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Front foot flat. Push through it and your hands. Stand. Stand still a moment.</td><td>Only with a sturdy chair and someone home</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push up. Earn the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>New knee, severe knee pain, or dizziness: skip the floor. Chair stands instead.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hands on the chair the whole time. Slow down. Up is a push, not a jump. **Easier:** Only the first step: lower into a half-kneel on the towel and come back up, holding the chair. Or skip the floor and do sit-to-stands. **Harder:** Iron: from kneeling, sit down onto the floor beside the chair, then roll to your knees and rise with the chair. Only with someone home.

**Safety callouts:** Only try the floor with a sturdy chair or sofa next to you and someone home. Recent hip or knee replacement, or severe knee arthritis: follow your surgeon's or physical therapist's guidance first. New knee? Kneeling may not be allowed yet. Ask your surgeon. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:05–9:50 · Heel raises

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel raises</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise up onto the balls of your feet, as high as is comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or rise halfway</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you rise.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like someone is pulling a string on top of your head. Weight over the big toe and second toe, not rolling out. **Easier:** Sit in your chair and raise your heels from there, or hold the counter with both hands and rise only halfway. **Harder:** One hand on the counter. Later: one leg at a time, with both hands on the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:50–10:35 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>10:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>10:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 10:35–11:10 · Cool-down breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>10:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>10:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 11:10–11:35 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>11:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>You practised the floor. That's the one people skip.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>11:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Earn the floor. Same time tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mobility | 9:10 | SET-LIVING | C-CASUAL | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuesday. Mobility. The back and the hips.</td><td>Day 16 · Mobility</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move with less stiffness. That's the goal. Nothing forced.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sharp pain or dizziness? Stop.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:05 · Ankle pumps

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:05–1:45 · Chest lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Chest lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your chest up toward the ceiling, growing tall.</td><td>Easier: Smaller lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Look straight ahead, not up.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you relax.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall. Look straight ahead, not up. **Easier:** Smaller lift. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–2:35 · Seated hinge

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hinge</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Keep your back long and tip your chest forward from the hips, sliding your hands toward your knees.</td><td>Easier: Smaller tip forward</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back, proud chest.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend at the hips, not the belly.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you sit tall.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Long back, proud chest. Bend at the hips, not the belly. **Easier:** A smaller tip forward. **Harder:** Hold a water bottle against your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:25 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn your chest to the right, only as far as comfortable. Eyes follow.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall first, then turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips stay still.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:25–4:25 · Standing hip-front stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Standing hip-front stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuck your tailbone under slightly and squeeze the buttock of the back leg.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stay tall. Don't arch your back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small movement, big squeeze.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stay tall. Don't arch your back. Small movement, big squeeze. **Easier:** Smaller step. **Harder:** Reach the arm on the back-leg side up toward the ceiling, to comfortable height.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:25–5:20 · Standing bird-dog

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Standing bird-dog</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your right foot back and lift it a few inches behind you, toes on or just off the floor.</td><td>Easier: Leg only, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. No arching.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Long back. No arching. Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg. **Easier:** Leg only; both hands stay on the counter. **Harder:** Hold the reach for three seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–6:05 · Wall slides

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wall in front of you or behind you. Chair nearby.</td><td>Wall slides</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your arms up the wall only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Walk fingertips up the wall</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ribs down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow and smooth.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you slide up, out as you slide down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Slow and smooth. **Easier:** Face the wall and walk your fingertips up it instead. **Harder:** Hold for two seconds at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:05–6:55 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rest your right ankle on your left knee, or as close as you can.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Relax the knee, don't push it.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:55–7:45 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, hands on your bent knee.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>A gentle stretch is enough.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:45–8:45 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:10 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stiff in the morning? Tomorrow, notice the first ten minutes. Tell me if it's easier by next week.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Same time tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>


# Session 17 · Wednesday: New steps

| Type | Length | Set | Wardrobe | Voices |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Balance | 8:45 | SET-KITCHEN | C-TRAIN-B | Chang |

<div class="box stop" markdown="1">

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wednesday. Balance. Four new steps today, all at the counter.</td><td>Day 17 · Balance</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoes on. Clear floor. Hand on the counter the whole time for anything new.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Dizzy? Sit down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:05 · Toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise onto the balls of your feet.</td><td>Easier: Heel raises in place</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Small steps. **Easier:** Heel raises in place instead. **Harder:** Hand hovering, still right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–2:55 · Heel walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your toes and walk on your heels, 10 small steps.</td><td>Easier: Toe lifts in place</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes up.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small steps. Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Toes up. Small steps. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** Toe lifts in place, holding the counter. **Harder:** 20 steps.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:55–3:55 · Step over a towel

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Step over a towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step over the towel sideways with the near foot, then the other.</td><td>Easier: Flat towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift the knee. Clear the towel.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Lift the knee. Clear the towel. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** A flat towel instead of rolled. **Harder:** Step over forward and back, still holding the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:55–5:05 · Heel-to-toe stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel touching toe.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes on something still at eye level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft knees. Tall head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly and steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–6:15 · One-leg stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to your left foot.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:15–7:05 · Backward walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand resting on the counter. Look behind you first. Path clear.</td><td>Backward walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Normal steps backward. Toe, then heel.</td><td>Easier: Five small steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Slow is correct.</td><td>Backward: hand stays on the counter</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hand stays on the counter. Slow. Look where you're going first. **Easier:** Five small steps. **Harder:** Ten steps, slower.

**Safety callouts:** Only ever with a hand resting on the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:05–7:50 · Sit-to-stand, no hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Sit-to-stand, no hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit with feet slightly narrower than usual.</td><td>Easier: Hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Find your balance at the top before you move.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Find your balance at the top before you move. Slow down. **Easier:** Use your hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Feet together.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:50–8:20 · Cool-down breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:20–8:45 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>New steps. You did all four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tonight: heel-to-toe while you brush your teeth. Hand on the sink.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Thursday. Carry and climb. Real life moves.</td><td>Day 18 · Strength</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stairs with a rail, a bag or two, and your chair.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on the stairs: stop, sit, call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle pumps first if you've been sitting. Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:45 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Five easy ones.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–3:25 · Power stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, feet flat, arms crossed or hands on thighs.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fast up, slow down.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:25–5:05 · Stair practice

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bottom of the stairs. Hand on the rail. The whole time.</td><td>Stair practice</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Whole foot on each step. Steady pace.</td><td>Easier: Bottom 3 steps only</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. Rest at the top as long as you like.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Whole foot on the step. Rail hand never lets go. **Easier:** Just the bottom 3 steps, up and down. **Harder:** Two flights, or carry a light bag in the free hand.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain or unusual breathlessness on stairs: stop, sit, and call your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:05–6:15 · One-side carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Free hand trails along the counter.</td><td>One-side carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean away from the bag.</td><td>Easier: Lighter bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall like a lamppost.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall like a lamppost. Shoulders level. **Easier:** A lighter bag, free hand on the counter the whole time. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or a longer walk.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:15–7:10 · Band pull-apart

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band pull-apart</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull the band apart toward your chest by opening your arms.</td><td>Easier: Hands wider on the band</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow on the way back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull apart.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shoulders down. Slow on the way back. **Easier:** Hands wider apart on the band (less tension), or the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Hands closer together, or a 2-second squeeze.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:10–8:05 · Curls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Curls</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend your elbows and bring the bottles toward your shoulders.</td><td>Easier: One arm, or empty bottles</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows stay by your sides.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>No swinging.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you curl up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows stay by your sides. No swinging. **Easier:** One arm at a time, or empty bottles. **Harder:** Heavier: a half-gallon jug (about 4 pounds), then a full gallon jug (about 8 pounds), one at a time.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:05–8:45 · Cool-down breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:45–9:10 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Carry and climb. That's groceries and grandkids.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow: breath and two new tai chi forms.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>
