### 0:35–2:05 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>

</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–2:55 · Holding up the sky

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Holding up the sky</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in and lift your hands slowly up the front of your body, turning palms to the ceiling as they pass your face.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow, like moving through warm water.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Look straight ahead.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as the hands rise, out as they come down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow, like moving through warm water. Look straight ahead. **Easier:** Sit and do it seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Rise onto your toes a little at the top, holding the chair back with one hand if needed.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:55–4:15 · Brush knee

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Near the fence. Feet hip-width. Soft knees.</td><td>Brush knee</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step forward, heel first. Hand brushes past the knee. Other hand pushes forward.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, feet together</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight moves slowly front. Breathe out as you push.</td><td>Short step, slow shift</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tai chi is slow balance practice: weight shifts, short steps, turning. Balance is one of the most trainable things there is.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step, not a lunge. Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, one hand on the counter. **Harder:** Four steps across the room and back, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:15–5:35 · Parting the horse's mane

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Parting the horse's mane</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Imagine holding a ball at your chest, right hand on top.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow like honey.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as the arm sweeps up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step. Slow like honey. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, holding the counter with one hand. **Harder:** Step forward across the room, left then right, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:35 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to the right foot while your right hand floats across in front of your face and your left hand floats low in front of your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:35–7:15 · Heel raise and slow lower

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hands on the counter. Up on the toes.</td><td>Heel raise and slow lower</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lower slowly. Iron can use a soft bump, if bones and joints allow.</td><td>Easier: Slow lower, no drop</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you rise, out as you lower.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall spine. Soft bump, never a stomp. **Easier:** Heel raise with a slow lower, no drop. **Harder:** Ten gentle drops.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today. Gentle impact. Skip it if you have osteoporosis without a training history, pelvic floor problems, or a joint replacement; do the heel raise without the drop instead.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:15–8:15 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sunday. Three weeks in.</td><td>Day 21 · Rest + stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Easy stretches, some on the bed, then your check-in.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Anything sharp? Stop.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–2:15 · Neck nods and half-turns

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Neck nods and half-turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly nod yes: look a little down, then back to level.</td><td>Easier: Even smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small and slow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chin stays level when you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small and slow. Chin stays level when you turn. **Easier:** Make the movement even smaller. **Harder:** Add a chin tuck: gently slide your chin straight back, making a double chin, hold two seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Dizzy with head movements? Keep it tiny, keep your eyes open, and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:15–3:05 · Knee rocks on the bed

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>On your bed. Sit down first, then lie back slowly.</td><td>Knee rocks on the bed</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let both knees drift gently to the right, only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: A tiny movement</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:34</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small and slow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders stay on the bed.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as the knees drift.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small and slow. Shoulders stay on the bed. **Easier:** A tiny movement, a few inches. **Harder:** Pause for one slow breath on each side.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:05–3:50 · Bed bridge

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>On your bed. Sit down first, then lie back slowly.</td><td>Bed bridge</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze your buttocks and lift your hips a few inches.</td><td>Easier: Squeeze without lifting</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push through your heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift with your buttocks, not your back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you lift.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Push through your heels. Lift with your buttocks, not your back. **Easier:** Just squeeze your buttocks without lifting. **Harder:** Hold three seconds at the top, or lift higher.

**Safety callouts:** Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:50–4:20 · Ankle pumps before standing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit up slowly. Ankle pumps. Ten.</td><td>Ankle pumps before standing</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand. Then stand slowly, holding something.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:20–5:15 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, hands on your bent knee.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>A gentle stretch is enough.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

<tr><td>7:35–8:30</td><td><strong>High wall sit</strong></td><td><em>Seated knee straightening:</em> 2 sets of 10 each leg</td><td>2 holds of 20 seconds</td><td>3 holds of 20 seconds</td><td>3 holds of 30 seconds</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:30–9:15</td><td><strong>Calf stretch</strong><br>Calf stretch at the wall</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td><td>20 seconds each leg</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:15–9:50</td><td><strong>Cool-down breathing</strong><br>Cyclic sighing</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td><td>35 seconds</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:50–10:15</td><td><strong>Close</strong></td><td colspan="4">All levels together</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Week four. Monday. Same moves, slower lowering.</td><td>Day 22 · Strength</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow on the way down is where strength grows.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Counter close. Chest pain, dizziness, sharp pain: stop.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle pumps first if you've been sitting. Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:45 · Easy sit-to-stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Five easy ones.</td><td>Easy sit-to-stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:45–3:45 · Legs

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Legs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Cross your arms over your chest, or rest your hands on your thighs.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Nose over toes.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Breathe in as you sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

**Safety callouts:** Advanced. Only if your knees feel good with step-ups.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:45–5:15 · Push

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Push</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lower your chest toward the counter edge.</td><td>Easier: Wall push-ups</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Straight line from head to heels.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Straight line from head to heels. Squeeze your buttocks so your hips don't sag. **Easier:** Wall push-ups. **Harder:** Lower slowly for three seconds. Later (Iron track): a sturdy low bench or bottom stair, only if the counter version is easy for 12 reps.

**Safety callouts:** Wrist pain? Make fists or hold the counter edge instead of flat palms.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:15–6:25 · Band row

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band row</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull your elbows back past your ribs.</td><td>Easier: Closer to the door, or towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Elbows close to your body.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall chest, shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Elbows close to your body. Tall chest, shoulders down. **Easier:** Sit closer to the door so the band is slacker, or do the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Scoot back for more tension, or pause 2 seconds with elbows back.

**Safety callouts:** Check the band for nicks before every use. Door must open away from you and be locked.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:25–7:35 · Suitcase lift

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Suitcase lift</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Push your hips back with a long back and bend your knees a little.</td><td>Easier: Lighter jug, higher surface</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips back. Long back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hips back. Long back. Don't lean toward the jug. Stay square. **Easier:** A lighter jug, and lift it from a higher surface like the counter's edge of a table. **Harder:** A heavier bag, or lift from the bottom step instead of the chair.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis: this is the safe bending pattern. Keep the back long, never curl. Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: long back always, never round to reach.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:35–8:30 · High wall sit

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back on the wall. A few inches down. Chair beside you.</td><td>High wall sit</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Keep talking. Count out loud with me.</td><td>Easier: Only 2 inches down, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>High blood pressure or a heart condition? Keep it short and ask your doctor about longer holds.</td><td>Keep breathing: count out loud</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shallow is fine. This is not a contest of depth. Knees stay behind or over your toes. **Easier:** Slide down only 2 inches, or hold for just 10 seconds. **Harder:** Slide a little lower (never below where your knees are bent to a right angle), or hold up to 30 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Breathe through it. High blood pressure or a heart condition? Ask your doctor before long holds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:30–9:15 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:15–9:50 · Cool-down breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>9:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:50–10:15 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>9:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow down. That's where it counts.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>10:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Same time tomorrow.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tuesday. Mobility. Shoulders, ankles, neck.</td><td>Day 23 · Mobility</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small, slow, comfortable.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sharp pain or dizziness? Stop.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Ankle pumps and circles

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Ankle pumps and circles</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Point your toes away, then pull them toward you. That's one pump.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow movements.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feel your calves work.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–1:55 · Chin tucks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Chin tucks</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your chin straight back, making a double chin. Keep your eyes level.</td><td>Easier: Smaller, 1-second hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide back, don't tip down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall neck.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:43</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slide back, don't tip down. Tall neck. **Easier:** Smaller movement, one-second hold. **Harder:** Hold five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:55–2:35 · Neck nods and half-turns

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Neck nods and half-turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly nod yes: look a little down, then back to level.</td><td>Easier: Even smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small and slow.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chin stays level when you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small and slow. Chin stays level when you turn. **Easier:** Make the movement even smaller. **Harder:** Add a chin tuck: gently slide your chin straight back, making a double chin, hold two seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Dizzy with head movements? Keep it tiny, keep your eyes open, and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–3:05 · Shoulder rolls

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Shoulder rolls</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your shoulders up toward your ears.</td><td>Easier: Just shrug and let go</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Big, slow circles, backward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Let your arms hang heavy.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you lift, out as you roll down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow circles, backward. Let your arms hang heavy. **Easier:** Just shrug up and let go. **Harder:** Add arm circles: small circles out to the sides, forward and back.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:05–3:55 · Wall slides

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wall in front of you or behind you. Chair nearby.</td><td>Wall slides</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your arms up the wall only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Walk fingertips up the wall</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ribs down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow and smooth.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you slide up, out as you slide down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Ribs down. Slow and smooth. **Easier:** Face the wall and walk your fingertips up it instead. **Harder:** Hold for two seconds at the top.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:55–4:45 · Calf stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Calf stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bend the front knee and lean gently toward the wall until you feel a stretch in the back calf.</td><td>Easier: Smaller step back</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Back heel stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Toes point forward.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:30</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly through the stretch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Back heel stays down. Toes point forward. **Easier:** Smaller step back. **Harder:** Bigger step back, or bend the back knee slightly to reach the lower calf.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:45–5:35 · Standing bird-dog

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Standing bird-dog</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your right foot back and lift it a few inches behind you, toes on or just off the floor.</td><td>Easier: Leg only, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long back. No arching.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you reach.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Long back. No arching. Squeeze the buttock of the moving leg. **Easier:** Leg only; both hands stay on the counter. **Harder:** Hold the reach for three seconds.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:20 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn your chest to the right, only as far as comfortable. Eyes follow.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall first, then turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips stay still.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:20–7:00 · Prayer and wrist stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit at the table. Forearm resting on it.</td><td>Prayer and wrist stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Press your palms together in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Smaller stretch, 10 s</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretch only.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Gentle stretch only. Shoulders down. **Easier:** Smaller stretch, 10 seconds. **Harder:** Hold 20 seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Carpal tunnel symptoms (numb, tingling fingers) that get worse: skip it and tell your doctor.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:00–8:00 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:00–8:25 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Loose shoulders, happy neck.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:13</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow, balance.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Wednesday. Balance. We put the new steps together.</td><td>Day 24 · Balance</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Counter for everything. Chair behind you.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Dizzy? Sit down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Weight shifts

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Weight shifts</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly shift your weight to your right foot. Pause.</td><td>Easier: Do it seated</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Feet stay flat on the floor.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:03</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your ankles and hips, like a tree swaying. Feet stay flat on the floor. **Easier:** Do it seated: shift your weight side to side on the chair. **Harder:** Make the shifts bigger, or let one hand hover.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:15 · Heel-to-toe walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Heel-to-toe walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward, placing your heel directly in front of the toes of the other foot.</td><td>Easier: Feet apart, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes forward, not down at your feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow is correct.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes forward, not down at your feet. Slow is correct. **Easier:** Walk with your feet slightly apart, not touching, holding the counter. **Harder:** Let your hand hover above the counter. Later: walk backward along the counter with one hand resting on it (normal steps).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:15–3:15 · Toe and heel walks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Toe and heel walks</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:27</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rise onto the balls of your feet.</td><td>Easier: Heel raises in place</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:37</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Small steps. **Easier:** Heel raises in place instead. **Harder:** Hand hovering, still right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** Calf cramps are common at first. Stretch and walk them out. One calf that is swollen, red and painful is not a cramp: that is for your doctor, today.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:15–4:10 · Step over a towel

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Step over a towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step over the towel sideways with the near foot, then the other.</td><td>Easier: Flat towel</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift the knee. Clear the towel.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:44</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Lift the knee. Clear the towel. Hand on the counter. **Easier:** A flat towel instead of rolled. **Harder:** Step over forward and back, still holding the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:10–5:20 · One-leg stand + reach

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>One-leg stand + reach</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to your left foot.</td><td>Easier: Toe stays on the floor</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly. Count out loud.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Don't lean on the counter. Squeeze the buttock of the standing leg. **Easier:** Just shift your weight onto one foot, keeping the other toe lightly on the floor. **Harder:** One hand hovering above the counter, then both hands hovering, right next to the counter.

**Safety callouts:** No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet. Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–6:10 · Backward walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand resting on the counter. Look behind you. Clear.</td><td>Backward walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Normal steps backward.</td><td>Easier: Five small steps</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:49</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Hand stays on the counter. Slow. Look where you're going first. **Easier:** Five small steps. **Harder:** Ten steps, slower.

**Safety callouts:** Only ever with a hand resting on the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:10–7:10 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to the right foot while your right hand floats across in front of your face and your left hand floats low in front of your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:41</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:10–7:40 · Cool-down breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit down. Two sniffs in through the nose. One long sigh out.</td><td>Cool-down breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:40–8:05 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Update the fridge chart.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:53</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tomorrow: strength and your mini check.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Thursday. Short strength today, then a mini check: 30-second chair stands and the balance stand.</td><td>Day 25 · Strength + mini check</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>A number that moves. Before your renewal date, you get to see it.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain, dizziness, sharp pain: stop.</td><td>Mini check: chair stands + balance</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:15 · Warm-up march

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ankle pumps first if you've been sitting. Stand slowly. Hand on the counter.</td><td>Warm-up march</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>March. Easy rhythm. Breathe steady.</td><td>Easier: Sit and march</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Stand tall. Knee up, foot down softly. **Easier:** Sit and do the seated march. **Harder:** Lift knees higher, march faster, or let one hand hover above the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:15–2:45 · Power stands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Power stands</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:32</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, feet flat, arms crossed or hands on thighs.</td><td>Easier: Normal speed, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:46</td><td>Chang</td><td>Fast up, slow down.</td><td>Advanced (Iron): not your starting point</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:55</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out hard as you stand.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Fast up, slow down. Quick is not the same as sloppy. Knees stay over toes. **Easier:** Normal-speed sit-to-stand with hands on your thighs. **Harder:** Hold a jug of water at your chest, or pause one second just above the seat on the way down.

**Safety callouts:** Stop the fast part if you feel dizzy when you stand. Go back to normal speed.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:45–3:35 · Band pull-apart

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit or stand with the chair behind you. Check the band first.</td><td>Band pull-apart</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Pull the band apart toward your chest by opening your arms.</td><td>Easier: Hands wider on the band</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow on the way back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you pull apart.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Shoulders down. Slow on the way back. **Easier:** Hands wider apart on the band (less tension), or the towel pull-apart. **Harder:** Hands closer together, or a 2-second squeeze.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:35–4:35 · Carry

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Clear path. Walk along the counter or a hallway wall.</td><td>Carry</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stand tall, shoulders down.</td><td>Easier: One light bag, hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall, like you're proud of the groceries.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short, steady steps.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steadily. You should be able to talk.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall, like you're proud of the groceries. Short, steady steps. **Easier:** One light bag, and keep your free hand trailing along the counter. **Harder:** Heavier: two full gallon jugs (about 8 pounds each). Iron track: two heavier bags or kettlebells.

**Safety callouts:** Hand arthritis flaring today? Squeeze gently, or skip and do the finger spread only. Pick up and put down with a hinge. Never round your back to lift.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:35–5:35 · Rest before the check

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit. Drink some water. One minute.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Arms crossed, or hands on thighs if you need them. Same way as day one.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Ready the timer. I'll count you in.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:35–6:35 · Mini check: 30-second chair stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair against the wall. Arms crossed.</td><td>Mini check: 30-second chair stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Three, two, one, go. Stand all the way up, sit all the way down.</td><td>Easier: Higher seat, hands on thighs</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:02</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you stand. Ten seconds left.</td><td>30-second chair stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Stop. Write your number.</td><td>Write your number</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Nose over toes. Knees point the same way as your toes. Don't let them cave inward. Sit down slow. Two or three seconds. **Easier:** Put a firm cushion or folded blanket on the seat to make it higher, or push up with your hands on your thighs or on chair arms. **Harder:** Arms crossed, lower for a slow count of three, and pause one second just above the seat before touching down. Later: hold a gallon jug of water at your chest.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:35–7:45 · Mini check: balance stand

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>At the counter. Hand hovering just above it. Grab it any time.</td><td>Mini check: balance stand</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hold up to ten seconds. The moment you touch the counter or move your feet, that's your time.</td><td>Easier: Half-step, both hands down</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe. Switch feet if you like. Write your best time.</td><td>Up to 10 seconds · grab the counter anytime</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Eyes on something still at eye level. Soft knees. Tall head. **Easier:** Half-step stance: front foot's heel beside the big toe of the back foot. Both hands on the counter. **Harder:** Lift one hand to hover just above the counter. Later: both hands hovering.

**Safety callouts:** Balance drills always start with support. Hands hover, they don't wander away from the counter. No barefoot drills on slippery floors, no socks on hard floors, no rugs under your feet.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:45–8:20 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

<tr><td>7:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Didn't move? Tired days happen. The full retest is day 30.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Muscle is a savings account. You've been depositing.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Friday. The whole flow. Everything you've learned, one after another.</td><td>Day 26 · Breath + qigong</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chair behind you. Slow like honey.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Light-headed or dizzy: sit.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–2:05 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–2:50 · Holding up the sky

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Holding up the sky</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in and lift your hands slowly up the front of your body, turning palms to the ceiling as they pass your face.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow, like moving through warm water.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:25</td><td>Chang</td><td>One... two... breathe out... three... slow down... four.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Look straight ahead.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as the hands rise, out as they come down.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow, like moving through warm water. Look straight ahead. **Easier:** Sit and do it seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Rise onto your toes a little at the top, holding the chair back with one hand if needed.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:50–3:35 · Drawing the bow

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Drawing the bow</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Bring both hands in front of your chest.</td><td>Easier: Seated, arms only</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:07</td><td>Chang</td><td>Knees over toes.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall through the top of the head.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you draw the bow, in as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Knees over toes. Grow tall through the top of the head. **Easier:** Sit tall in your chair and do the arm movement only. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more (never below comfortable).

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:35–4:20 · Separating heaven and earth

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Separating heaven and earth</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Lift your right hand up past your face and press the palm toward the ceiling, to comfortable height.</td><td>Easier: Seated, to shoulder height</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>One hand reaches up, one presses down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Long spine.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in as you separate, out as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** One hand reaches up, one presses down. Long spine. **Easier:** Seated, or lift only to shoulder height. **Harder:** Slower, with a longer out-breath.

**Safety callouts:** Shoulder pain or a known rotator cuff problem? Only lift to a comfortable height, or skip it.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:20–5:00 · Looking back

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Looking back</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn your palms outward and slowly turn your head to look over your right shoulder, only as far as comfortable.</td><td>Easier: Turn the eyes more</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chin level.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shoulders stay down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:48</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn, in as you return.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chin level. Shoulders stay down. **Easier:** Turn your eyes more than your head. **Harder:** Hold the turn for one slow breath.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles. Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:00–5:45 · Punching with a steady gaze

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Punching with a steady gaze</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slowly punch your right fist forward, turning it palm down.</td><td>Easier: Seated, same arm movement</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:17</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow punch. This is not boxing.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:24</td><td>Chang</td><td>Eyes steady and focused.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you punch.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slow punch. This is not boxing. Eyes steady and focused. **Easier:** Seated, same arm movement. **Harder:** Bend your knees a little more, keeping them over your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:45–6:40 · Brush knee

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Brush knee</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Step forward with the left foot, heel first, into a short stance.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, feet together</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step, not a lunge.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:14</td><td>Chang</td><td>Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:23</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you push forward.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step, not a lunge. Weight moves slowly from back foot to front foot. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, one hand on the counter. **Harder:** Four steps across the room and back, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 6:40–7:35 · Parting the horse's mane

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>6:40</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Parting the horse's mane</td></tr>
<tr><td>6:51</td><td>Chang</td><td>Imagine holding a ball at your chest, right hand on top.</td><td>Easier: Arms only, hold the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Short step.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:09</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slow like honey.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>7:18</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as the arm sweeps up.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Short step. Slow like honey. **Easier:** Arms only, feet together, holding the counter with one hand. **Harder:** Step forward across the room, left then right, near the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 7:35–8:35 · Cloud hands

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>7:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hand on the counter. Chair behind you.</td><td>Cloud hands</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Shift your weight to the right foot while your right hand floats across in front of your face and your left hand floats low in front of your belly.</td><td>Easier: Seated, or one hand on counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>7:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>8:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly; no need to match the breath to the moves.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Move from your waist and legs, not just your arms. In tai chi we call it sinking: really, it's lowering your center of mass. Soft knees. **Easier:** Keep one hand on the counter and move the other hand only. **Harder:** Add a small side step with each shift, next to the counter.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 8:35–9:35 · 4-6 breathing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>8:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>4-6 breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose for a count of 4.</td><td>Easier: In for 3, out for 4</td></tr>
<tr><td>8:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly rises first.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Soft shoulders.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>9:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>In for 4, out for 6. That is about 6 breaths a minute. No holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Belly rises first. Soft shoulders. **Easier:** In for 3, out for 4. **Harder:** Continue for 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, go back to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 9:35–10:00 · Close

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Saturday. A longer steady walk today, with Sun.</td><td>Day 27 · Walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Flat route. Indoors counts.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest pain or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, call your doctor.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–2:35 · Easy walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Easy walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Easier: Indoors, touching the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Walk at an easy pace for 2 minutes to warm up.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:26</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Arms swing naturally.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:58</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe easy and steady. The talk test: you should be able to speak in short sentences.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:35–6:35 · Steady walk

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Good shoes. Cane or walker if you use one.</td><td>Steady walk</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>Steady pace. Tall. Arms swing.</td><td>Easier: Indoors, touching the counter</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:54</td><td>Chang</td><td>Can talk, can't sing.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:33</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sun, you're ahead of me.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:11</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe steady.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>6:27</td><td>Sun</td><td>Walk faster, old man.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

</div>

</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Heel, roll, push. Tall. Eyes ahead. **Easier:** Normal-length steps, hand on the counter. **Harder:** 20 steps, a little faster.

**Cues:** Tall. Eyes ahead, not at your feet. Arms swing naturally. Heel, then toe. **Easier:** Walk indoors: kitchen to front door and back, touching the counter as you pass. Or march seated. **Harder:** Add 1-minute faster stretches, or a gentle hill.

**Safety callouts:** Chest pain, pressure, or unusual breathlessness: stop, sit, and call your doctor. If it doesn't settle in a few minutes, call 911.

## Script

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:00</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sunday. Four weeks. A month.</td><td>Day 28 · Rest + stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gentle stretches, then a look back at your month.</td><td>Stop if chest pain, dizziness or sharp pain</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:21</td><td>Chang</td><td>Anything sharp? Stop.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:35–1:35 · Cyclic sighing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>0:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Cyclic sighing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe in through your nose.</td><td>Easier: Just slow nose breathing</td></tr>
<tr><td>0:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Two sniffs in, one long sigh out.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>No holding at any point.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:16</td><td>Chang</td><td>The out-breath is always longer than the in-breath. No breath holds.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Two sniffs in, one long sigh out. No holding at any point. **Easier:** Just breathe slowly through your nose, making the out-breath a little longer. **Harder:** Build up to 5 minutes.

**Safety callouts:** If you feel light-headed, return to normal breathing.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 1:35–2:05 · Chin tucks

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>1:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Chin tucks</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:42</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide your chin straight back, making a double chin. Keep your eyes level.</td><td>Easier: Smaller, 1-second hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>1:47</td><td>Chang</td><td>Slide back, don't tip down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall neck.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>1:57</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe normally.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Slide back, don't tip down. Tall neck. **Easier:** Smaller movement, one-second hold. **Harder:** Hold five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Nods and half-turns only. Never full neck circles.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:05–2:50 · Gentle seated turn

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:05</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Gentle seated turn</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:15</td><td>Chang</td><td>Turn your chest to the right, only as far as comfortable. Eyes follow.</td><td>Easier: Smaller turns</td></tr>
<tr><td>2:22</td><td>Chang</td><td>Grow tall first, then turn.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:29</td><td>Chang</td><td>Hips stay still.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>2:36</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you turn.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Grow tall first, then turn. Hips stay still. **Easier:** Smaller turns. **Harder:** Place one hand on the opposite knee as a light guide. Never pull into the turn.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis? Turn gently and only as far as comfortable. Never force the twist.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 2:50–3:45 · Seated hamstring stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>2:50</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Seated hamstring stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:01</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall, hands on your bent knee.</td><td>Easier: Lean only an inch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:10</td><td>Chang</td><td>Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:19</td><td>Chang</td><td>A gentle stretch is enough.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>3:28</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Chest proud. Bend from the hips, not the back. A gentle stretch is enough. **Easier:** Lean only an inch or two. **Harder:** Pull your toes toward you a little more.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep the back long. Never curl down toward your toes.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 3:45–4:35 · Figure-4 hip stretch

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>3:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit tall. Chair against the wall.</td><td>Figure-4 hip stretch</td></tr>
<tr><td>3:56</td><td>Chang</td><td>Rest your right ankle on your left knee, or as close as you can.</td><td>Easier: Ankle on shin, or skip crossing</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:04</td><td>Chang</td><td>Tall back.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:12</td><td>Chang</td><td>Relax the knee, don't push it.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Tall back. Relax the knee, don't push it. **Easier:** Rest the ankle on your shin instead of your knee, or skip crossing and just let the knee drop out a little. **Harder:** Hinge forward a little farther with a long back.

**Safety callouts:** New hip? Follow your surgeon's precautions first.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 4:35–5:20 · Pelvic tilt on the bed

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>4:35</td><td>Chang</td><td>On your bed. Sit down first, then lie back slowly.</td><td>Pelvic tilt on the bed</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:45</td><td>Chang</td><td>Gently flatten your lower back into the mattress by tightening your belly.</td><td>Easier: Smaller, one-second hold</td></tr>
<tr><td>4:52</td><td>Chang</td><td>Small movement.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>4:59</td><td>Chang</td><td>Belly tightens, bottom stays down.</td><td></td></tr>
<tr><td>5:06</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe out as you flatten.</td><td></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Small movement. Belly tightens, bottom stays down. **Easier:** An even smaller movement, one-second hold. **Harder:** Hold five seconds.

**Safety callouts:** Osteoporosis or a past spine fracture: keep it small and gentle. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 5:20–5:50 · Ankle pumps before standing

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td>5:20</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit up slowly. Ankle pumps.</td><td>Ankle pumps before standing</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:31</td><td>Chang</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand. Then stand slowly, holding something.</td><td>Easier: Smaller movements</td></tr>
<tr><td>5:39</td><td>Chang</td><td>Breathe slowly.</td><td>Sit a moment before you stand</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Cues:** Big, slow movements. Feel your calves work. **Easier:** Smaller movements. **Harder:** Lift one foot off the floor while you circle.

**Safety callouts:** Great before you stand up from sitting or lying. Sit a moment before you stand, then stand slowly while holding something steady.

</div>

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

<div class="seg" markdown="1">

### 0:00–0:35 · Welcome

<table class="small script"><thead><tr><th>Time</th><th>Who</th><th>Spoken</th><th>On screen</th></tr></thead><tbody>
